Repeatability: the check hands a checker a procedure with a concrete operation - take this baseline sentence, paste it under another scenario, ask whether it is still true - so two checkers run the same experiment rather than exercising taste.

findings.description: FAIL, but on a new and narrower defect than r1's - the mechanism is now right and the reason it is right holds up. I re-derived r1's correction rather than taking it: scope-decisions.md:3 scopes the reference to 'flagging a memory or journal candidate during phase 3', :9-19 is the content-signal table that picks the token, and SKILL.md:126 restates the same content test in the phase 3 prose ('project is the floor; client requires recurrence across projects or stakeholder-level facts; journal requires generalization beyond this client'). The path walk at SKILL.md:30-35 picks the phase 1 scope root, a different thing. r0 was wrong, r1 was right, and the rewrite adopted the correct mechanism. The clause's narrowing to one non-textual signal is also correct, and I checked it row by row: of the nine rows at :11-19, eight are readable off the inbox file and only :15 ('Subject entity has already been referenced in 2+ projects' notes at this client') needs evidence outside it, which is exactly why :29-35 gives it a grep. What fails is the selection procedure the check hands the checker, and it fails by contradicting the case the clause itself mandates. (1) The check ends with a flat rule - 'A scenario whose input carries a client-tier signal while expecting the project token fails' - and the clause requires 'At least one case exercises the narrowest-scope tiebreak: when signals conflict, the narrower proposal is the correct one.' The canonical tiebreak, and the one scope-decisions.md:23 is written to demonstrate ('Project is the floor'), is a project-versus-client conflict expecting the project token. That case carries a client-tier signal and expects the project token, so C-7's own final sentence fails the case C-7's own text requires. (2) The contradiction is not confined to the tiebreak scenario, because the text requires all three inputs to be ones that 'could plausibly have gone elsewhere' - that is, to carry more than one tier's signal - while the check asks a checker to confirm 'the expected tier must be the one that table selects.' The table at :9-19 does not select anything for a multi-signal input; the rule that selects is Conflict Resolution at :21-25, which the check never names. So the check points the checker at :9-19 and withholds the section that decides. Two checkers will split on the project scenario specifically: one applies :23 and passes it, one applies C-7's last sentence and fails it, on the same artifact. (3) Smaller, same clause: the recurrence requirement says the references must sit 'in distinct project directories', but scope-decisions.md:32's grep is `<client-root>/{pursuits,projects}/*/notes/` and :35 counts hits in distinct project directories under it. A fixture with `clientA/foo/notes/` and `clientA/bar/notes/` satisfies the clause's wording and is invisible to the documented grep, so the signal it grades still would not exist. Fix, all three in one edit: make the selection procedure the table at :9-19 plus Conflict Resolution at :21-25; replace the flat final sentence with the qualified one it meant ('a scenario whose input carries a client-tier signal and no project-tier signal while expecting the project token fails'); and write the recurrence layout as the grep's own shape, `<client-root>/{pursuits,projects}/<project>/notes/`, in two or more distinct project directories.

findings.description: FAIL, on the residue of r1's finding rather than on r1's finding, which is genuinely closed. The revision adds the empirical test r1 asked for and it is correctly grounded - I verified `--tier2-extract` at migrate-scope.sh:365-377 writes `$tier2_extract_dir/$note_id.extract.md`, that it is gated to the non-record branch (SKILL.md:384, 'Records get no extract; Tier 2 is a note concept'), that v1-ness is the gate (`has_schema_key` at :157-164, skip at :324-327), and that the run is safe to perform mid-job: the dirty-tree refusal at :135-146 is conditioned on `apply == 1`, and `--tier2-extract` refuses to combine with `--apply` (:126-130), so a checker running it against a committed fixture writes only into the directory it passes. The attribution half is also right - `tier2-entity-unsourced` is the migrator's entity-only diagnostic, and SKILL.md:388's 'The apply enforces the half it can' is exactly what the clause now says. What still fails is that neither half of the check is bound to the note the scenario grades. (1) The existence test asks the checker to 'confirm it writes at least one `<note-id>.extract.md`'. A fixture holding one v1 note and two `schema: 2` notes emits exactly one extract and passes that test, while a scenario whose rows grade one of the v2 notes has no extract behind it - the same unfalsifiable rows r1 diagnosed, reached by a mixed fixture instead of an all-v2 one. (2) The row test - 'Confirm every row in the scenario is decidable by reading the extract' - still does not say whose extract, and it is sequenced before the run, so a checker can satisfy it against an extract transcribed into EVALS.md and then satisfy the existence test separately against the extractor's real output. Nothing joins the two, so a doc quoting an illustrative extract that does not match the emitted one passes. The clause text already says the right thing ('against the note's emitted extract'); it is the check that does not reach it. Fix: name the invocation and the binding in one move - run `bash inbox-to-memory/scripts/migrate-scope.sh <fixture> --tier2-extract <scratch-dir>`, confirm `<scratch-dir>/<id>.extract.md` exists for the note id the scenario names, and grade every row of that scenario against that file.

findings.description: FAIL, on a coverage gap the rewrite left rather than on r1's contradiction, which is closed. I confirmed the closure: the exemption now names `eval-scope.sh`, `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/` paths, and the eval fixture directory names explicitly, so the C-1/C-9/C-10 triple that r1 showed was jointly unsatisfiable is satisfiable again, and the exemption is a written rule rather than a charitable reading. The failing example still fails a real artifact for the stated reason - `[memory candidate: journal]` is undefined, because journal candidates take no scope token (SKILL.md:106, machine-contracts.md:72). The gap is in the enumeration that survived the rewrite. C-9 quantifies over 'Every piece of the skill's own vocabulary the doc cites' and then fixes that phrase in apposition to a closed list: candidate-flag tokens, phase numbers, frontmatter keys, `status` values, `memory_type` values, memory folder names, lint failure codes, and script paths. The skill's inline token vocabulary is larger than 'candidate-flag tokens'. SKILL.md's own 'Candidate Flag Taxonomy' at :93-101 contains five forms, and the authoritative registry is a ten-row grammar table at machine-contracts.md:63-79, whose other five rows are the ones this suite is built on: Tension, Open question, Open question resolved, Decision. C-6 requires a whole scenario written in `[tension: unacknowledged]`, and its fixture turns on `[open question: <slug>]`. Neither is a candidate-flag token. So a worker who writes `[tension: unresolved]` or `[open question pending:]` into a pass condition invents vocabulary the skill does not emit, and the clause built to catch precisely that is enumerated past it. That is C-9's own stated harm - 'worse than no eval, because it fails work that was correct' - arriving through the enumeration rather than through the exemption. The split is under-inclusive rather than false-failing, so a charitable checker catches the defect and a literal one does not, which is the same checker-to-checker disagreement r1 failed the clause for, one category over. Fix: replace 'candidate-flag tokens' with the registry itself - every inline token registered in the grammar table at `references/machine-contracts.md:63-79`, which is the table the skill declares authoritative ('A token shape absent from this table is a lint failure on a v2 file').

findings.description: FAIL, and this is a clause r1 passed - the fresh sweep found it, not the revisions. r1's finding is closed and I confirmed it: the existence gate ('First confirm a run-procedure section exists and names `eval-scope.sh`; if there is no such section this clause fails outright') removes the empty-set vacuity r0 diagnosed, and I agree with r1 that one named section beats repeating staging steps per scenario. The new hole is that the script half of the check verifies only the negative. It asks the checker to 'run `eval-scope.sh` against one fixture and confirm it prints the staged path, writes only beneath a scratch directory, and leaves `git status --porcelain` unchanged.' A script that prints `/tmp/i2m-eval.XXXX` and copies nothing satisfies every term: it prints a path, it writes only beneath a scratch directory (writing nothing is a subset of that), and it leaves git untouched. So the deliverable C-1 calls the fixture-staging script can stage no fixture and still clear the only clause that executes it. This is the well-formed-but-useless shape at the level of the script rather than the fixture, and it matters here because C-10 is the sole owner of eval-scope.sh's behavior - C-1 owns only its path and C-13 only its comments, so nothing else in the constitution would notice. The clause text already states the positive requirement ('copies a named fixture into a fresh scratch directory outside the repo and prints that path'); the check drops the copy. Fix: after running it, confirm the printed directory contains that fixture's `_inbox/` and its `_memory/` or `entries/` marker - the same opt-in test C-3 applies to the committed original - so the staged copy is verified to be a copy. Separately I overturn r1's other note on this clause: r1 said 'leaves `git status --porcelain` unchanged' should say before-versus-after rather than empty. 'Unchanged' already means before-versus-after; there is nothing to fix.

Six non-goals, none of which blocks a criterion: staging is not scoring, so 'no graded runner' leaves eval-scope.sh reachable; 'no execution' matches C-12's empty table; 'no scaffold mode' narrows the surface without touching a criterion; the stale-inventory non-goal at :110 records the user's decision and names the consequence for a well-meaning worker ('a worker that updates them fails that clause'), which is how a non-goal should be written. One loose edge survives from r0 and r1 and I confirm it a third time, still at low stakes: the first non-goal says a skill defect 'is filed as an issue, not fixed here', which authorizes an external side effect (`gh issue create`) that no clause constrains and that check-diff-scope.py structurally cannot see, since it only reads the working tree. It is nearly dead because this job never executes the suite, so no scenario can expose a defect during the job. Saying 'staged as a draft under `state/`' rather than 'filed' closes it for free and matches what prior runs in this repo actually did.
